method: Thesis exposure = sum over open theses of posterior x value-pool weight (mandatory infrastructure 1.0, pricing power / scarce 0.9, abundant -0.3, new risk -0.6, loses pricing power -1.0). Final = exposure x (0.5 + opportunity/100) x (1 + gap/100) x technical readiness (trend template) x attention (not-priced +15%, crowded -20%). 'ready' = passes the book's entry gate today.

picks.why: Highest thesis exposure in the set (8.31) and the only name carrying the 97.5%-posterior electrons thesis in three roles at once — firm dispatchable generation gaining pricing power, generation/electrical equipment scarce, and nuclear/SMR supply chain scarce — plus pricing-power roles under T-003 (80%) and T-002 (76%). Fundamentals are mid-pack (reality 59) but pricing is only 51 against narrative 76, giving a positive expectations gap of +8: the story is loud, the multiple is not yet fully extended. Attention at 29 with no crowding flag says the marginal buyer has drifted away while the causal case strengthened.
picks.entry_condition: Currently basing/downtrend with technical_ready=false — wait for a reclaim of stage-2 structure (technical score moving off 50 toward 85+) or buy a first tranche only on confirmation of the T-004 next signal: a >=1GW hyperscaler campus contracting firm generation ahead of interconnection.
picks.key_risk: T-004's own stated invalidator — a neocloud or vendor-financed GPU default shrinking the order pipeline — would hit GEV's gas and grid backlog hardest, and the basing technical suggests someone already suspects it.

picks.why: Carries the labour-scarcity pools directly: T-007 at 90.2% posterior (repair/retrofit gaining pricing power, skilled trades scarce) and T-006 at 83.5% (crew-owning specialty contractors as the aggregation point for scarce human capital), with T-004 EPC exposure on top. Unlike the mega-cap industrials it still has a positive expectations gap (+3, pricing 58 vs reality 61) and is already in a stage-2 uptrend at technical score 88. Narrative and attention are both null — nobody is writing about it, which is exactly why a crew-owning contractor with pricing power is still available at reality-level pricing.
picks.entry_condition: Technically ready now; buy on a pullback that holds the stage-2 trend, and add on the late-October specialty-contractor prints if backlog duration extends past 18 months with craft labour named as the binding constraint.
picks.key_risk: T-006's falsification path — backlog shortening or a disclosed data-centre cancellation — converts scarcity rent into crew release fast, and a small-cap contractor with no analyst following de-rates violently on one soft backlog number.

picks.why: Sits in six theses simultaneously, four of them as mandatory_infrastructure (agent authorization under T-001, consolidated enterprise platforms under T-002 at 76%, attestation for local inference under T-004 at 97.5%, biometric governance under T-005 at 87.8%) plus scarce custody/key-management under T-008. Crucially it is the only one of the security cluster not already overpriced: expectations gap +2 with pricing 73 against reality 74, versus CRWD at -20 and PANW at -18 for identical thesis exposure. Technical score 100, stage-2, attention only 40 and not crowded — you get the same causal exposure as the crowded names without paying the premium.
picks.entry_condition: Ready; initiate on trend continuation, size up only if Q4 FY2026/Q1 FY2027 disclosures show agent-governance priced as a separate line rather than bundled free.
picks.key_risk: T-002's explicit deflation branch — if platforms bundle agent governance free to win consolidation deals, security becomes volume without price, and FTNT's gap of +2 offers almost no cushion.

picks.why: The widest mispricing in the set: expectations gap +42 with pricing at 12 against reality 54, while holding pricing-power and scarce roles across T-002 (identity/fraud-graph data scarce, risk pricing and certification scarce, 76%), T-001 (liability absorption for agent error gaining pricing power) and T-008. If agent-initiated commerce needs underwriting and certification, this is the toll both theses route through. The market is pricing it as a broken scoring monopoly, not as the risk-pricing layer of delegated transactions.
picks.entry_condition: Technical score 0, basing/downtrend — do not front-run. Require a stage change (technical score above 60) or the T-001 April-cycle signal: a top-10 issuer or top-3 network publishing agent-transaction liability and chargeback-parity rules.
picks.key_risk: Pricing of 12 usually encodes a real structural threat — mortgage-score competition and regulatory pressure on the scoring franchise can impair the cash engine long before the agent-liability pool monetises, and the chart says that process is still underway.

picks.why: Best fundamental quality in the list (reality 83) with a still-positive expectations gap of +15 and three high-posterior roles: scarce identity/fraud-graph data and pricing-power sovereign/on-prem AI under T-002 (76%), scarce agentic interfaces to finance and mandatory compliance/surveillance for 24/7 markets under T-008 (80.3%), and the workflow systems-of-record that agents must act through under T-001. Thesis exposure is lower (4.01) but it is concentrated in the layers where delegation and tokenised settlement both require an audited system of record.
picks.entry_condition: Ready, stage-2, technical 88 — enter on continuation but keep initial size small given attention at 52, the highest in the set; add on the T-008 signal of a top-five venue publishing tokenised-equity volume with named market makers.
picks.key_risk: Attention 52 with pricing 69 means sentiment, not cash flow, sets the clip size; any multiple compression in high-expectation software hits this before the thesis is ever tested.

picks.why: The only cheap way to own the two highest-conviction consumer layers: T-004's endpoint inference silicon gaining pricing power and trust/attestation for local inference as mandatory infrastructure (97.5% posterior), plus T-001's credential custody and the identity/preference graph as scarce. Expectations gap +9 with pricing 58 against reality 67 and narrative 69 — the market is paying for a hardware cycle, not for custody of the delegation layer. Attention 31, not crowded, technical score 100 in a stage-2 uptrend.
picks.entry_condition: Ready; accumulate on trend, with the explicit add trigger being the T-001 tell — Apple shipping an OS agent with stored payment authority on by default.
picks.key_risk: Apple has repeatedly been the slowest to ship agentic capability; if delegated authorization standardises off-platform, the credential-custody role migrates to networks and issuers and the thesis contribution collapses to just silicon.

picks.why: Identical thesis exposure to IESC (5.63; T-007 at 90.2%, T-006 at 83.5%, plus T-004 EPC scarcity) but priced at 40 against reality 48 for a +8 expectations gap — the cheapest entry into the skilled-trades scarcity pool. It is the laggard of the contractor complex precisely because it has no narrative score and no attention reading, while the causal case for crew-owning aggregators is among the best-evidenced in the thesis set.
picks.entry_condition: Basing/downtrend, technical_ready=false — require a stage-2 breakout or buy only after the late-October contractor prints confirm backlog duration extending past 18 months with explicit field-wage escalation clauses.
picks.key_risk: Mechanical EPC is the most data-centre-levered of the contractors; a single disclosed project cancellation (not an Oracle-style delay) is T-006's named falsifier and would reprice backlog quality immediately.

picks.why: Same six-thesis security exposure as FTNT and CRWD (5.47) but the lowest pricing in that cluster at 47 against reality 57, giving a +10 expectations gap while CRWD, PANW and NET all sit between -16 and -20. Narrative 77 with attention 48 and no crowding means the story is already written and the price has not followed — the inverse of its peers.
picks.entry_condition: Technical stage is 'emerging' at 62, not yet ready — wait for confirmation into stage-2 (score 85+) before initiating; a positive gap in a basing name is cheap for a reason until the trend turns.
picks.key_risk: Reality score of 57 is the weakest in the security group; if platform consolidation under T-002 favours the broad suites, the point-solution loses the attach-rate fight and the discount proves justified rather than temporary.

memo.portfolio_note: This list is two concentrated bets with a hedge against each. Bet one is the physical constraint on AI: GEV, IESC and EME all route through T-004 (97.5%) and T-006/T-007 skilled-trades scarcity, and they share a single falsifier — a neocloud or GPU-financing credit event that converts scarcity rent into crew release and backlog cancellations. That is roughly half the book's risk in one causal node, so GEV and EME are deliberately held as unconfirmed watch positions pending stage changes, with only IESC technically ready to carry size. Bet two is security and delegation: FTNT, ZS, PLTR, AAPL and FICO all draw on T-001/T-002/T-008, and the selection rule inside that cluster was purely the expectations gap — FTNT (+2) and ZS (+10) in, CRWD (-20), PANW (-18), NET (-16) out despite identical thesis exposure, because paying 89 pricing for 68 reality is buying the thesis after the market has. FICO is the asymmetry trade (+42 gap, pricing 12) and is sized as an option, not a position, until its chart stops confirming the bear case. Three things would rewrite this list: agent-governance being bundled free in the Q4 FY2026/Q1 FY2027 security disclosures (cuts the entire T-002 leg and takes FTNT/ZS out), a GPU-financing default (removes GEV, IESC, EME together), and the April 2027 card-network rulebook cycle passing without an agent-liability rule (collapses the T-001 contribution to FICO and AAPL).
